question.knowledge_point: Calculating the Sum of a Complex Number and Its Conjugate
question.worked_solution:
**Method 1**

When we add a complex number and its conjugate, the result is always twice the real part of the complex number.

For the given complex number $z=-9-\text{i},$ the real part is $Re(z)=-9,$ so we have

$$
\begin{aligned}z+\overset{―}{z} & =2\text{Re}(z) \\  & =2(-9) \\  & =-18.\end{aligned}
$$

**Method 2**

Alternatively, we can actually carry out the process of adding the complex number and its conjugate.

To obtain the conjugate of the complex number $z=-9-\text{i},$ we flip the sign of the imaginary part and get $\overset{―}{z}=-9+\text{i}.$

Adding, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}z+\overset{―}{z} & =(-9-\text{i})+(-9+\text{i}) \\  & =(-9+(-9))+\text{i}(-1+1) \\  & =-18+\text{i}\cdot 0 \\  & =-18.\end{aligned}
$$
